summary: Indonesia is a brutal, high-complexity economic game about shipping, manufacturing, and mergers, where companies grow through takeovers and compete for scarce shipping capacity across the archipelago. It's a cutthroat, long-form economic simulation known for its punishing depth and lack of hand-holding.
praised: strong sense of building a shipping/manufacturing empire
criticised: punishing for new players against experienced ones
auctions and route control can feel cutthroat

interaction.kind: auction-driven economic competition on a shared map
interaction.detail: Companies, ports, and shipping routes all sit on one shared map, and controlling a zone or route can lock out competitors' goods movement. Shares and company mergers are won through open bidding against the whole table, so much of the tension comes from auctions rather than acting directly on an opponent's pieces.

subsystems: corporate ownership/shares economy (single integrated engine covering production, shipping, and company value)
scoring.how_you_win: Each round players auction for turn order and take a role (production, shipping, entrepreneur, etc.) to grow companies and move goods for income; when a production track fills up the game ends and whoever holds the most total wealth (cash plus share value) wins.
